summary: Cape Sarichef Airport (WSF/PACS) is a small remote airfield situated on the western tip of the Alaska Peninsula near the Unimak Island area. It primarily serves the surrounding region, which has historical ties to early Russian exploration and World War II military operations. The airport supports limited general aviation and provides access to one of the most remote parts of the Alaskan coastline.
faqs:
Q: What is Cape Sarichef Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport serves general aviation purposes, providing access to the remote Cape Sarichef area on the Alaska Peninsula.

Q: Are there commercial flights to Cape Sarichef Airport?
A: No scheduled commercial service operates to this small airfield; access is typically via private or charter aircraft.

Q: Where exactly is the airport located?
A: It is situated on the Alaska Peninsula in southwestern Alaska, near Unimak Island and the Aleutian Island chain.

Q: What is the significance of the Cape Sarichef name?
A: The cape is named after Russian navigator Gavril Sarychev, and the area also hosted a WWII-era military installation.
transport_tips: Access to Cape Sarichef Airport is limited to air travel, typically requiring a charter or private aircraft. The nearest community with broader transportation links is Cold Bay, located nearby with its own regional airport. Weather conditions in this region can be unpredictable, so flexible travel plans are essential.
local_tip: Given the area's notoriously volatile weather with frequent fog and high winds, always check marine and aviation forecasts together—conditions at nearby Unimak Pass often dictate whether the strip is flyable, even when local skies appear clear.
